draft.title: Technician
draft.position_summary: Provides technical assistance to IT Client Services technical staff with maintaining and upgrading the distributed Audio/Video (AV) systems on campus (e.g., instructional classrooms, lecture theatres and meeting spaces) in preparation for the next semester. Aids in the cleaning and maintenance of AV equipment (e.g., projectors, AV racks, audio equipment) for the Burnaby Campus and Fraser International College. Aids in upgrading and reimaging computing hardware and software within AV systems. Ensures that all facilities, equipment, software, documentation, and signage are maintained in proper order.

duties.statement: Ensures that all facilities, equipment, software, documentation, and signage are maintained in proper order. Detects existing or potential problems and failures and reports them to senior technicians. Performs data entry by entering details of errors/problems into the departmental trouble reporting database (i.e., Confluence). Removes equipment for repair and records items into the inventory system (i.e., Confluence)

Inspects and tests AV Services computing equipment using diagnostic software and electronic test equipment (i.e., digital multimeters); analyzes information provided by the manufacturer and/or procedure manual; and identifies system faults or maintenance required (i.e., component replacement or repair). Analyzes and corrects computing equipment malfunctions by ensuring that standardized configuration is maintained on all lab computers as required

Keeps work areas clean and tidy by storing equipment, materials, and supplies in their assigned areas, and by using various cleaning tools and products to ensure an organized and clean working environment

Maintains AV equipment (i.e., data projectors, overhead projectors, etc.) by replacing lamps, cleaning filters and upgrading settings. Replaces defective system components with upgraded AV equipment (i.e., projector lamps and filters, wireless microphone components, batteries, etc.) using basic hand tools (i.e., screwdrivers, pliers)

Performs maintenance and cleaning of computing hardware and accessories by replacing defective mice, keyboards, and monitors and cleaning computer monitors, keyboards, mice, etc., using standard cleaning tools
Performs other duties and responsibilities consistent with the job description and classification on request

Resolves minor hardware and software problems (i.e., broken lavalier cords or filters, damaged projector components, updating & reimaging computers, etc.) ﻿by referring to the appropriate resources (i.e., service desk knowledge database). Refers complex problems to senior technicians

internal: Information Technology Professional III, IT Services
external: List internal and external contacts (i.e., specific positions within own department, other departments, students, faculty, on/off campus vendors, etc.), the duration of each contact (i.e. less than 1 hour at a time, 1-2 hours at a time, more than 2 hours at a time), and the frequency of each contact (i.e. occasional, frequent, or continuous).

qualifications.text: High school graduation and general courses or training of moderate duration (one semester equivalent) in computing technology or a related field
Ability to exercise mature judgment and to work independently
Ability to follow oral and written instructions accurately
Ability to perform minor repairs and maintenance on audio visual equipment (i.e., replacing projector lamps, filters, etc.)
Ability to record data using a standard inventory recording database (e.g., Confluence, etc.)
Ability to troubleshoot and resolve minor hardware and software problems (i.e., microphone component issues, projector problems, computer upgrades)
Ability to use a variety of hand tools (screwdrivers, pliers, etc.) to replace defective system components
Good analytical reasoning and problem solving skills
Good interpersonal and communication (oral and written) skills
Good knowledge of computers and operating systems (i.e., PCs, Macs, Windows)
Good knowledge of projection systems (i.e., data projectors and overhead projectors), audio systems (i.e., wired and wireless microphones, mixing boards, audio processors)
Ability to lift, move, or carry heavy equipment or materials up to 20 kg
Ability to work flexible hours including evenings and weekends

model.title: Audio/Visual Technician
model.position_summary: Provides technical assistance to IT Services staff in the maintenance, upgrade, and operation of campus audio/visual (AV) systems and associated computing equipment. The role ensures that AV facilities, equipment, software, documentation and signage are kept in proper order, conducts inspections and testing, performs minor repairs, and resolves hardware and software issues. By maintaining clean work environments and accurate inventory records, the technician supports instructional spaces, meeting rooms, and other university facilities while delivering reliable AV services during flexible hours, including evenings and weekends.
